Unblocks Carter's hands-on step for **APRV-379**. The task is blocked on a fact recorded nowhere in this repository: the shape of the `item/started` notification that carries a file change. The probe already saw those frames and kept one boolean about them, so the correlation would have been written against a guess, and a guessed shape matches nothing silently.

## What the probe does now

- **Stores every item notification verbatim.** `item/started`, `item/updated` and `item/completed` go through the same `redact` walk into a per-trial `item_notifications` array, each entry `{ at, method, item_type, carries_content, verbatim }`. The old `item_started_with_content` boolean stays, computed by the same predicate so the two cannot drift.
- **Adds a sixth trial, `approve-patch`.** The existing prompt let the model satisfy its patch instruction with a shell redirection, which produces a command item and no file change at all. The new prompt asks for the marker file to be created with the file editing tool and forbids the shell for it. The trial is deliberately outside the leak, hold and void verdict logic: `approve` remains the only positive control, and the four refusal trials are measured against exactly what they were before.
- **Records which file-change API arrived.** Legacy inline change set, item-based `itemId`, both, or unknown, read from the request's own key paths rather than from its method name. That is the second fact APRV-379 needs.
- **Prints it.** `--report` gains the item-notification lines per trial (methods, item types, whether any carried content), the API form line, and the verbatim file-change frame itself, so the shape is readable without opening results.json. A run that captured none says so in those words rather than printing an empty heading.

## What Carter runs, from the primary

```
node scripts/probes/codex-app-server.mjs --setup
node scripts/probes/codex-app-server.mjs --run
node scripts/probes/codex-app-server.mjs --report
```

No new flag: `--run` does all six trials. `--run --trial approve-patch` spends one billable turn instead of six, and the report then prints VOID for the APRV-349 interception verdict because the approve control did not run, which is correct and says nothing about this capture. The same three commands and what to paste back are in APRV-379's implementation notes; the task stays To Do, and AC1 still wants the shape written into `docs/codex-app-server-bridge.md` after the run.

## Tests

`tests/probe-codex-app-server.test.ts`: the stub server now reads the prompt it was sent, so the patch-only prompt reaches a file-change item with no command item in front of it, and the end-to-end test asserts the stored frame, the item type, the API form and the three new report sections. Five new unit tests cover `itemType`, `fileChangeApiForm` (item-based, legacy inline, both, unknown, and a command request), `isFileChangeItem`, the report's captured and NONE branches, and the per-trial prompt. No test contacts a real server.

Probe suite: 14/14, exit 0. Build, typecheck and lint clean. Full `npm test` locally: 4765 pass, 27 fail, all pre-existing and unrelated (18 SMTP/email on Node v26, which refuses an IP `servername` on STARTTLS; 9 packaging tests that need a `node_modules` in the worktree and pass after `npm ci`). CI on Node 22 is the truth.

No SPEC, schema or policy change. The probe is not a gate and decides nothing.
